title: Wholesome Girlies vs Period Calendar: Fertile Window Tools
description: Compare Wholesome Girlies and Period Calendar for fertile days, reminders, ads, price in Nigeria and what happens to your dates when you change phone.
share: If you are choosing between Period Calendar and Wholesome Girlies, this comparison shows the reminders, ads, Nigerian prices and what happens to your saved dates.
kicker: For women choosing a period tracker while trying to conceive
answer: If you want reminders and a place to note your symptoms and moods every day, use Period Calendar. If you want to see your fertile days without signing up or seeing ads, use Wholesome Girlies. Type the day your last period started, and your fertile days show on the same screen. You can also print a list of questions for your fertility doctor, and send your husband a checklist of what he can do for his sperm health. No calendar app can tell you the exact day you ovulate, ours included. Ours counts days from your last period, and we show you the count below.

doctor: See a doctor after twelve months of trying, or six months if you are over 35. See one sooner if your cycles are very irregular, shorter than 21 days or longer than 35, or have stopped. Take your last three or four period dates with you.

how.title: How the Wholesome Girlies calculator works
paras: The Ovulation and Fertile Window Calculator uses two numbers: the first day of your last period and your usual cycle length. It adds the cycle length to that date to find your next period, then counts back 14 days to estimate the day you ovulate. The fertile window it shows starts five days before that day and ends one day after it.

On a 28-day cycle, day 1 is the first day of your period. Your next period is due on day 29, ovulation is estimated on day 15, and the window runs from day 10 to day 16. The Period Tracker then replaces the cycle length you typed with your own average once you have logged three period starts.

A calendar estimates and does not detect. A Journal of Medical Internet Research analysis of 7,043 tracked cycles found that ovulation does not sit reliably at the midpoint of a cycle, and the National Health Service says it usually happens 10 to 16 days before your next period. Period Calendar's temperature, mucus and test records add signals ours does not use, so we do not claim ours predicts better.

faq.q: What does Period Calendar cost in Nigeria?
faq.a: On the Nigerian App Store, in-app purchases run from ₦500 (about $0.40) for 7 days of Premium to ₦69,900 (about $52) for Pro: Period Calendar. Removing the ads alone is ₦4,900 (about $4). Google Play marks the app as containing ads and in-app purchases.

faq.q: Does Period Calendar need an account?
faq.a: Not to log. Its App Store listing says you can use the app without creating an account. Backing up and restoring on a new phone uses a Google account or an email.

faq.q: Can Wholesome Girlies remind me before my period?
faq.a: Yes, through your own phone calendar. After the Period Tracker or Ovulation Calculator shows your result, tap Add to my calendar. Your next three periods, your fertile days and your likely ovulation day go into your calendar, with a reminder 2 days before. We do not send reminders by push or email.

faq.q: Does the Wholesome Girlies calculator predict better than Period Calendar?
faq.a: We do not claim that. It sets ovulation 14 days before your next period and the window from five days before to one day after. Period Calendar describes a method that also uses temperature, mucus and test records. A calendar predicts. It does not detect. Take your last three or four period dates to a clinician.

Wholesome Girlies keeps them on your phone, and the forget button clears them. Period Calendar explains what it collects in its privacy policy and Google Play data safety page. We show both sources here.
